title: Senior Manager — Technical Diligence and Programme Control
description:
Senior Manager \- Technical Due Diligence \& Project Monitoring \| Vantrock Real Assets \| Mumbai
 



 We want a civil engineer who started on the developer or contractor side, carried a site, then moved into technical due diligence or independent engineer work. Depth first, structure second. A site tells you what it will cost long before a contractor does.
 




 ABOUT VANTROCK
 




 Vantrock is an independent real assets platform. Real assets only. We start where we know the ground: logistics, warehousing and industrial parks, across the full chain \- first mile, last mile, city\-centre, dark\-store and self\-storage, and logistics\-anchored mixed\-use. From there, in sequence and only as each is delivered: industrial plots; suburban campuses, GCC and back\-office space; strata offices; and, in parallel, data centres and senior living.
 



 The platform was founded by Anshul Singhal, Founder \& CEO, who has built every platform he led as if it were his own \- three times over, on other people's capital. This is the fourth build, on his own. Across his career that record runs to 52 million sq ft delivered, 32 million as developer and 20 million as contractor, over 2,000 acres acquired and all of them litigation\-free, and more than 200 buildings. Delivered across the founder's three prior platforms. The board is chaired by Shailesh V. Haribhakti. The platform runs on Vantrock Intelligence, its own AI\-native operating layer.
 




 WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
 




 Read a site badly at diligence and the error is baked into the underwriting for the life of the asset. Read it well and the deal either improves or dies early, the cheapest outcome available. The same skill, pointed at a contractor's programme, tells you whether the date on it is real.
 



 Vantrock currently buys both judgements from consultants, one assignment at a time, with nobody inside who can mark their work. The pipeline is 10 million sq ft and ground breaks on the first 2 million in January 2027\. From that point the platform is running acquisitions and construction at once, and whoever can walk a site in the morning and take apart a Primavera file in the afternoon becomes the most useful person in the room.
 




 WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 




 \- Technical pre\-diligence on every site under consideration \- ground, levels, access, power, drainage, existing structures, and every physical constraint that changes what can be built there. Your output goes into the underwriting as a technical view with the assumptions stated.
 



 \- The buildability and cost\-shape read. Not a BOQ, a judgement: what makes this site expensive, and where the foundation cost goes.
 



 \- Drawing review at concept stage, against what actually builds, before it is a tender.
 



 \- Programme review and claims. Take apart the contractor's and the PMC's programmes and report what is real. Assess extension\-of\-time claims on merit.
 



 \- Technical validation on site: running bills, measurement, quality and progress against the drawings, with the record captured into Vantrock Intelligence.
 



 \- Command of technical partners: geotechnical agencies, surveyors, TDD firms, inspection agencies, PMCs. You never take a report on trust because it came on letterhead.
 




 THE CAREER SHAPE, AND THIS ONE IS NOT NEGOTIABLE
 




 We are looking for a specific arc, in a specific order. You started on the developer's or the contractor's side. You carried responsibility on a site, and you know what a delay costs because you have been the person who had to explain it. Then you moved into technical due diligence, lender's independent engineer, technical audit or advisory work, where you learned to structure a problem, write for an executive, and hold more than one project in your head at a time.
 



 The order matters more than either half. Someone who has only ever consulted can build a governance framework nobody on the ground respects, because it asks for things a site cannot give. Someone who has only ever been on site can hold a project but not a portfolio. We want depth first and structure second, and we want both.
 



 Bring the first half in detail. We will ask which sites, what your scope was, what the ground turned out to be and what it cost to deal with.
 




 QUALIFICATION
 




 \- A full\-time B.E. or B.Tech in Civil Engineering. This one is not negotiable and no other discipline substitutes.
 



 \- A postgraduate qualification is a strong plus rather than a requirement: NICMAR (ACM, APM or the QSCM diploma), RICS School of Built Environment, an IIT or NIT M.Tech in structural, geotechnical or construction engineering, and NMIMS MBA (Tech.) Civil Engineering with Operations Management. An MBA in Finance, a CFA or CA is an added advantage.
 




 TECHNICAL GROUNDING \- ESSENTIAL
 




 This is the part of the seat that cannot be learned on the job here, so we will test it directly, on a real drawing set.
 



 \- Ground and land form. Borelogs, SPT data, safe bearing capacity, settlement, water table, ground\-improvement options. Contours, cut and fill, approach gradients, and survey output read rather than taken on trust. You know what to specify to a geotechnical agency before they mobilise.
 



 \- Codes and authorities. IS 456, 800, 875 and 1893, the National Building Code, and the authority rules that bind a site \- MIDC, HSIIDC, KIADB.
 



 \- Warehousing and industrial specifics. Pre\-engineered buildings, portal frames, crane gantries, floor loading and flatness to the occupier's standard, and what an insurer's engineering requirements do to a design.
 



 \- Services and cost. HT power, sanctioned load, distance to substation, water, sewage treatment, storm water outfall. BOQ, rate analysis, running account bills, variations, escalation, retention, defect liability. You can look at a rate and say whether it is real.
 



 \- Programme and drawings. Primavera P6 or MS Project at critical\-path, float and resource\-loading level, and extension\-of\-time claims assessed on merit \- essential in this seat, because reading a programme against physical reality is the job. GFC review, structural and services coordination, BIM clash detection at a level where you know what the model hides.
 



 \- Writing. A TDD report a lender's or an investment committee can act on, plus advanced Excel and PowerPoint.
 



 \- Platforms. MS Project at working level, plus SAP, Primavera P6 or Project Online.
 




 RELEVANT EXPERIENCE
 




 \- 8 to 12 years, the majority of it on or around sites rather than in a design office.
 



 \- At least three years on technical due diligence, independent engineer, technical audit or project monitoring work. Not delivery with a diligence assignment attached once.
 



 \- Sites assessed across greenfield land and built assets both. Assessing only completed buildings is half the seat.
 



 \- One constraint you found that nobody else had, and what it changed. This is the question the whole interview turns on.
 




 WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT
 




 \- Not delivery or EPC, and not design. Execution is owned elsewhere and that seat is filled; you review what is proposed, you do not draw it.
 



 \- Not the deal, and not portfolio governance. Investments owns underwriting; the register sits with the EPMO Lead. You supply the technical view into both, even when it kills the deal.
 




 HOW YOU WILL WORK
 




 Deliberately small, no departments. Survey, soil investigation, third\-party inspection and measurement all go to specialist agencies. What stays inside is the judgement about whether their work is any good. Expect to be on site most weeks, and expect your written view to be read by the founder, the investment committee and, in time, by lenders.
 




 THE WORK IS YOURS TO DO
 




 We are not building an army. You do the work rather than receive, route and report on it. The coordination, inside the platform and outside it with consultants, agencies, lenders and authorities, is done by you in person, on the phone and on site. You run your own tech stack rather than specifying it for someone else. Seniority changes what you are accountable for, not whether you roll up your sleeves.
 




 CULTURAL FIT
 




 We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co\-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
 



 Two requirements stand behind that and apply to every seat here. AI proficiency: every candidate takes the Vantrock AI Proficiency Test, supervised, regardless of seniority. Partner command: consultants, contractors, auditors, valuers, law firms and system vendors do a great deal of Vantrock's work, and everyone here is expected to command that work rather than defer to it.
 




 COMPENSATION
 




 Benchmarked against the upper quartile for the role and market, weighted toward equity, with performance\-linked incentives and ESOPs. We discuss numbers in the first conversation rather than anchoring either side prematurely.
 




 HOW WE WILL ASSESS
 




 An AI interview, reviewed before your CV. The AI Proficiency Test. A site round: a real site, or a real drawing set and soil report, and you tell us what you see. That round decides it. Two references. Five working days to hear back, and every conversation is confidential.
 




 TO APPLY
 




 Write to careers@vantrock.com, subject line "VR\-45 Senior Manager, Technical Diligence \- \[your name]". Four things: your CV, with the site half of your career set out as clearly as the advisory half; one artefact you personally wrote, redacted as you must, with three sentences on what you found that nobody else had; your current fixed compensation, expectation and notice; and one short paragraph naming the single site constraint you have seen change a deal most, and how you would have caught it earlier. That paragraph matters more than the CV.
 



 We don't hire roles. We build the platform.

 The platform was founded by Anshul Singhal, Founder \& CEO, who has built every platform he led as if it were his own \- three times over, on other people's capital. This is the fourth build, on his own. Across his career that record runs to 52 million sq ft delivered, 32 million as developer and 20 million as contractor, over 2,000 acres acquired and all of them litigation\-free, and more than 200 buildings. Delivered across the founder's three prior platforms. The board is chaired by Shailesh V. Haribhakti. The platform runs on Vantrock Intelligence, its own AI\-native operating layer.
 




 WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
 




 Ground breaks on the first 2 million sq ft of a 10 million sq ft pipeline in January 2027\. From that day the platform is running land, approvals, design, procurement, construction, leasing, operations and corporate initiatives at once, in several markets, with a deliberately small team.
 



 Right now every initiative reports to the founder in a different format on a different rhythm. That works at ten, not at fifty, and fifty is where this platform is by the end of next year. Filled well, the founder stops being the integration layer. Filled badly, we have added a reporting bureau.
 



 It is the senior of three seats, and the seat the Chief of Strategy and EPMO is most likely to be filled from. The EPMO Lead beneath you builds and runs the machine. The Senior Manager for Technical Diligence holds the ground truth under both. You hold the office's authority: the sequencing, the benefits at platform level, and every escalation that reaches the founder and the board.
 




 WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 




 \- The framework's authority. The EPMO Lead establishes the framework, operating rhythm, standards, stage gates and escalation protocols. You approve them, hold them when a project wants an exception, and are the reason they are respected across ten functions.
 



 \- Portfolio prioritisation and sequencing. Which initiatives run, in what order, against what capital and capacity. Project and non\-project, core and ancillary. The judgement the founder currently makes alone.
 



 \- Benefits realisation at platform level. Every initiative carries a stated operational, financial or customer benefit. You are accountable for whether the portfolio delivers them, and for killing those that will not.
 



 \- Transformation. Operational excellence, process improvement, cost optimisation and digital enablement, scoped by you and delivered through the office.
 



 \- Escalation to the founder and the board. The exceptions that matter, early, with options attached. A flag without an option is a complaint.
 



 \- Command of programme partners. You appoint them, set the standard they are held to, and replace them when they fail. Site\-level planning goes to a PMC reporting in, never to a seat on the roll.
 



 \- Building the bench. Two seats now, a third on trigger. Coach project and functional teams so the discipline survives you being on leave.
 




 THE CAREER SHAPE, AND THIS ONE IS NOT NEGOTIABLE
 




 We are looking for a specific arc, in a specific order. You started on the developer's or the contractor's side. You carried responsibility on a site, and you know what a delay costs because you have been the person who had to explain it. Then you moved into consulting, advisory or programme management, where you learned to structure a problem, write for an executive, and hold more than one project in your head at a time.
 



 The order matters more than either half. Someone who has only ever consulted can build a governance framework nobody on the ground respects, because it asks for things a site cannot give. Someone who has only ever been on site can hold a project but not a portfolio. We want depth first and structure second, and we want both.
 



 Bring the first half in detail. We will ask which projects, what your scope was, what went wrong on your watch and what it cost.
 




 QUALIFICATION
 




 \- A full\-time bachelor's degree in engineering \- Civil preferred and read first, Mechanical and Electrical read seriously \- or in Architecture or Construction Management.
 



 \- A postgraduate qualification in construction, infrastructure or project management. Programmes we know well: NICMAR (ACM, APM, REUIM), RICS School of Built Environment, CEPT, an IIT or NIT M.Tech, NMIMS MBA (Tech.) Civil with Operations Management.
 



 \- PMP, PRINCE2 or MRICS is an added advantage and not a substitute for either half of the arc.
 



 \- A finance qualification, and on this seat a requirement rather than an advantage: an MBA in Finance, a CFA, or CA. The office sequences capital as well as programmes, and whoever holds it reads a project's money as fluently as its schedule.
 




 TECHNICAL GROUNDING \- ESSENTIAL
 




 \- Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. The analysis and the executive pack are the product of this seat, and we will test both.
 



 \- Project controls, scheduling, cost monitoring, risk management and governance, understood well enough to challenge a schedule, a budget, a forecast or a progress claim and be right.
 



 \- Commercial and contract capability across procurement, consultant engagements, variations and claims, and fluency in a bill of quantities, a rate analysis and a running account bill from the site half of your career.
 



 \- Microsoft Project at working level, and a background working in at least one of SAP, Primavera P6 or Project Online. We will ask which one and what you actually did in it.
 



 \- Structured problem\-solving, and report writing an executive can act on without a meeting.
 




 RELEVANT EXPERIENCE
 




 \- 15 to 20 years across real estate development, construction or capital projects, with the arc above visible in it.
 



 \- Portfolio monitoring across multiple concurrent construction projects: controls, management reporting and risk governance. Give us the size in initiatives, square feet or crores, sites and states.
 



 \- Transformation or process improvement delivered to a measured benefit, and a governance function you built rather than inherited.
 



 \- One occasion where you told a chief executive or a board something they did not want to hear, early, with the options already worked out.
 




 WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT
 




 \- Not a delivery or EPC seat. Execution and construction delivery are owned elsewhere and that seat is filled. You review a programme; you do not build to it.
 



 \- Not financial planning and analysis. Forecasting and budget red flags sit in finance.
 




 HOW YOU WILL WORK
 




 Deliberately small, no departments. The doctrine before any addition is outsource first, then automate, then hire, and it applies to your own function as much as anyone else's. What stays inside is judgement, relationships, negotiation and accountability. You will sit next to the founder, and what arrives is the ambiguous part.
 




 THE WORK IS YOURS TO DO
 




 We are not building an army. You do the work rather than receive, route and report on it. The coordination, inside the platform and outside it with consultants, agencies, lenders and authorities, is done by you in person, on the phone and on site. You run your own tech stack rather than specifying it for someone else. Seniority changes what you are accountable for, not whether you roll up your sleeves.
 




 CULTURAL FIT
 




 We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co\-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
 



 Two requirements stand behind that and apply to every seat here. AI proficiency: every candidate takes the Vantrock AI Proficiency Test, supervised, regardless of seniority. Partner command: consultants, contractors, auditors, valuers, law firms and system vendors do a great deal of Vantrock's work, and everyone here is expected to command that work rather than defer to it.
 




 COMPENSATION
 




 Benchmarked against the upper quartile for the role and market, weighted toward equity, with performance\-linked incentives and ESOPs. We discuss numbers in the first conversation rather than anchoring either side prematurely.
 




 HOW WE WILL ASSESS
 




 An AI interview, reviewed before your CV. The AI Proficiency Test. A supervised practical on a real Vantrock initiative. Two references. Five working days to hear back, and every conversation is confidential.
 




 TO APPLY
 




 Write to careers@vantrock.com, subject line "VR\-21 Vice President, EPMO \- \[your name]". Four things: your CV, with the site half of your career set out as clearly as the advisory half; one artefact you personally designed, with three sentences on what was hard about it; your current fixed compensation, expectation and notice; and one short paragraph naming one thing in this description you think is wrong, and what you would do instead. That paragraph matters more than the CV.
 



 We don't hire roles. We build the platform.

title: Payment Lifecycle Manager - Vice President

 As a Payment Lifecycle Manager III within Payments Operations, you will be a key player in the firm's payment processing operations, leveraging your deep knowledge of payment lifecycle principles and practices. You will be responsible for managing a diverse team, driving automation initiatives, and developing new technologies to streamline processes. Your role will involve interpreting customer needs, identifying trends, and generating innovative solutions to enhance our operational efficiency and resilience. You will also be instrumental in managing stakeholder relationships, ensuring cybersecurity, and implementing anti\-fraud strategies. Your advanced proficiency in strategic planning, project management, and change management will be crucial in leading the team towards achieving our long\-term goals.
   

  

**Job Responsibilities**
* Lead teams responsible for end\-to\-end operational processes within the payments lifecycle, overseeing daily operations, setting objectives, managing escalations, and ensuring quality, risk, control, and compliance standards are upheld.
* Utilize deep knowledge of products and payments to interpret customer needs, identify trends, and implement innovative solutions that enhance payment operations processes, leveraging AI and automation for efficiency and compliance.

* Demonstrate accountability by quickly identifying and articulating issues, collaborating with stakeholders to assess risk and manage activities affecting the production environment, and prioritizing resolution.
* Foster an inclusive culture by enhancing employee engagement, attracting and developing talent, and applying advanced coaching and mentoring skills to promote professional growth and high\-quality service delivery.


**Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills**
* Demonstrated ability in operations leadership or management within payments, with at least seven years of experience leading high\-performing teams to achieve business priorities and objectives.
* Advanced knowledge of global payment processing operations, market products, systems architecture, and industry regulations to support operational efficiency, change management, and transformation.
* Proficiency in strategic planning and execution, including implementing automation technologies to optimize payments processing across global and cross\-functional departments.
* Skilled in data analysis techniques, capable of interpreting and communicating insights to inform decision\-making with senior stakeholders, while applying a commercial and growth mindset in fast\-paced environments.
* Strong interpersonal skills to optimize relationships and collaboration with stakeholders and cross\-functional teams, managing projects, solving problems, and driving continuous improvement initiatives.
* Understanding of cybersecurity controls and anti\-fraud strategies to identify and prevent potential threats, ensuring the protection of information and systems, with a proven track record in enhancing customer experience.


**Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills**

Morgan and Chase brands. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

 J.P. Morgan's Commercial \& Investment Bank is a global leader across banking, markets, securities services and payments. The Commercial \& Investment Bank provides strategic advice, raises capital, manages risk and extends liquidity in markets around the world.
